key_insight: A generalised particle–fluid model predicts how flows entrain particles from static beds across settings ranging from underwater vehicles to lunar landers, Martian drones and dust devils.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support CFD prediction of particle-cloud onset and formation around vehicles operating near loose sediment or dust.
method: Extend an existing helicopter-brownout entrainment model through targeted changes to modelling assumptions.
Define a measure of particle-cloud formation potential and outline integration into existing CFD software.
Adapt the model for swirl-free flows, gravity-sensitive small rotorcraft and updraft-driven dust devils.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical predictions, including a critical onset height for swirl-free cases, but provides no experimental validation or quantitative accuracy results.
watch_item: Applicability depends on scenario-specific modelling assumptions; CFD integration is outlined rather than demonstrated in the abstract.
paper_title: Bathyspheres, dust devils, lunar plumes and Martian drones: a generalised mathematical model for particle-fluid flow fields generated by static particle bed entrainment across macroscopic scales
